purpose: Binimetinib is used to treat a type of skin cancer called melanoma that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is specifically used in patients whose cancer has a certain gene change called a BRAF mutation. It is almost always used together with another medication called encorafenib.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a faulty gene that sends signals telling them to grow out of control. Binimetinib works by blocking a specific protein called MEK, which is part of that faulty signaling pathway. By blocking this protein, the medication helps slow down or stop cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Fatigue and tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, swelling in your hands or feet, rash or skin changes, muscle aches, stomach pain, changes in blood test results including liver and blood count changes, and increased sensitivity to sunlight.
warnings: This medication can cause serious eye problems — tell your doctor right away if you notice any vision changes or eye pain. It can also cause heart problems, lung problems, skin reactions, and bleeding. It may harm an unborn baby, so use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen. Regular check-ups, blood tests, and eye exams are needed during treatment.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 45 mg (two 15 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose and your next dose is more than 6 hours away, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 6 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose.
